# Set Up

## Load Libraries

```{r library}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(emmeans)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(knitr)
})

base_dir <- rprojroot::find_root(
  rprojroot::has_dir("AD_CR_HRS"), path = getwd()
)
analysis_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "AD_CR_HRS")
code_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "code", "R")
save_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "analysis-results", "ADNI")
plot_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "analysis-results", "plots")
```

# Define Functions

Most functions live in source files under `code_dir`, grouped by role. None of
them read objects from the global environment; everything a function needs is
passed in as an argument.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `plot_functions.R` | Spaghetti and scatter plots, panel labels, captions, colors, and PDF saving |
| `table_functions.R` | P-value and summary formatting, Spearman correlations, and the Low-vs-High comparison tables |
| `prediction_functions.R` | Reference values for covariates and the adjusted (emmeans) predictions |

## Source Files

```{r source_functions}
source(file.path(code_dir, "plot_functions.R"))
source(file.path(code_dir, "table_functions.R"))
source(file.path(code_dir, "prediction_functions.R"))
```

## Participant Data and Checks

These stay in this file because they are short and guard the data used below.

```{r func_participants}
# One row per participant: the earliest modeled visit.
get_baseline_rows <- function(model_df) {
  model_df %>%
    dplyr::arrange(.data$RID, .data$time) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(.data$RID, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

check_finite_mrs <- function(participants) {
  if (any(!is.finite(participants$mrs_z))) {
    stop("MRS comparisons require a finite mrs_z for each model participant.")
  }
}

# Do not silently plot a simplified model if fixed-effect columns were dropped.
check_models_estimable <- function(models) {
  for (group_name in names(models)) {
    if (anyNA(lme4::fixef(models[[group_name]], add.dropped = TRUE))) {
      stop(
        group_name, ": the Reduced Model has non-estimable fixed effects. ",
        "Inspect the subgroup covariate variation before making predictions."
      )
    }
  }
}
```

# Load Data

```{r load_results}
prep_ls <- readRDS(file.path(save_dir, "ADNI_Split.rds"))
mrs_model_df <- prep_ls$mrs_model_df
mrs_participants <- prep_ls$mrs_participants
mrs_median <- prep_ls$mrs_median
mrs_levels <- prep_ls$mrs_levels
mrs_datasets <- prep_ls$mrs_datasets
mrs_group_summary <- prep_ls$mrs_group_summary

model_ls <- readRDS(file.path(save_dir, "ADNI_Models.rds"))
sf_low <- model_ls$sf_low
sf_high <- model_ls$sf_high
```

The group summary below (from file 1) shows the observed predictor range in
each MRS group; it is the predictor-range table referred to in the plotting
sections.

```{r show_group_summary}
knitr::kable(
  mrs_group_summary, digits = 3,
  caption = "Participants, usable visits, and predictor ranges in each MRS dataset"
)
```

# Spaghetti Plot for the Two MRS Groups

Gray lines and points show observed participant memory trajectories.
Colored lines show adjusted mean trajectories from each MRS dataset's own
Reduced Model at the pooled participant-level **25th, 50th, and 75th
percentiles of baseline pTau**. These common display values are on the
original pTau scale. If quantiles coincide, identical curves are shown once.
Shading shows pointwise 95% confidence intervals for the adjusted mean.

For predictions, continuous MRS is held at the participant-level median
**within that MRS group**. Both panels use the same reference values for
age, sex, APOE4, and education. Each panel's fitted curves stop at its maximum
observed follow-up. The predictor-range table above and the warning below
identify any pTau display values outside a group's observed range.

## Reference Values

```{r reference_values}
reduced_models <- setNames(list(sf_low, sf_high), mrs_levels)
check_models_estimable(reduced_models)

reference_values <- get_reference_values(mrs_participants, mrs_datasets)
ptau_display <- get_ptau_display_values(mrs_participants)

knitr::kable(
  make_ptau_quantile_table(ptau_display),
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Common baseline pTau values used for adjusted trajectories"
)
```

## Predictions

```{r predictions}
memory_predictions <- make_memory_predictions(
  reduced_models, mrs_datasets, reference_values, ptau_display, mrs_levels
)
```

## Plot Inputs

```{r plot_inputs}
spaghetti_panel_labels <- make_spaghetti_panel_labels(
  mrs_group_summary, mrs_levels
)
memory_predictions <- add_panel_column(
  memory_predictions, spaghetti_panel_labels
)
observed_plot_df <- mrs_model_df %>%
  add_panel_column(spaghetti_panel_labels) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(.data$RID, .data$time)

ptau_colors <- get_ptau_colors(ptau_display$labels)
plot_caption <- make_spaghetti_caption(reference_values)
```

## Plot

```{r spaghetti_by_mrs_group, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
spaghetti_memory <- make_spaghetti_memory_plot(
  observed_plot_df, memory_predictions, ptau_colors, plot_caption
)
spaghetti_memory
```

## Save Spaghetti Plots as PDF Files

The combined two-panel figure and separate Low MRS and High MRS figures
are saved in `plot_dir` when this chunk runs. All three retain the
adjusted trajectories from the subgroup Reduced Models. The separate
figures use common x- and y-axis limits for comparison.
The combined figure is 14 x 8 inches; each separate figure is 10 x 8 inches.
Larger margins and additional spacing separate the panels, labels, legend,
and caption in both the HTML output and the PDFs.

```{r save_spaghetti_pdfs}
spaghetti_pdf_paths <- c(
  Combined = file.path(plot_dir, "ADNI_spaghetti_memory_low_high_MRS.pdf"),
  `Low MRS` = file.path(plot_dir, "ADNI_spaghetti_memory_low_MRS.pdf"),
  `High MRS` = file.path(plot_dir, "ADNI_spaghetti_memory_high_MRS.pdf")
)

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = spaghetti_pdf_paths[["Combined"]],
  plot = spaghetti_memory,
  device = grDevices::pdf,
  useDingbats = FALSE,
  width = 14,
  height = 8,
  units = "in"
)

axis_limits <- get_shared_axis_limits(observed_plot_df, memory_predictions)
single_panel_caption <- wrap_caption(plot_caption, width = 85)

for (group_name in mrs_levels) {
  group_spaghetti <- make_group_spaghetti_plot(
    group_name, observed_plot_df, memory_predictions,
    ptau_colors, single_panel_caption, axis_limits
  )

  ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = spaghetti_pdf_paths[[group_name]],
    plot = group_spaghetti,
    device = grDevices::pdf,
    useDingbats = FALSE,
    width = 10,
    height = 8,
    units = "in"
  )
}
```

# Scatter Plots of MRS and Baseline pTau

Each point represents one modeled participant. Spearman correlations are
computed separately in the high and low MRS datasets. The
trend line is an unadjusted ordinary least-squares line with a 95% confidence
band. The correlation and trend line describe association within each
group's restricted MRS range.

The two panels share the y-axis. Each panel's x-axis ends at the MRS cutoff (the
median): the Low MRS panel stops at the cutoff and the High MRS panel starts
there. This removes the empty region that would otherwise separate the panels,
which exists only because the groups are defined by that cutoff.

## Spearman Correlations

```{r mrs_ptau_spearman}
scatter_participants <- get_baseline_rows(mrs_model_df)
spearman_results <- compute_spearman_by_group(scatter_participants, mrs_levels)

knitr::kable(
  format_spearman_table(spearman_results),
  caption = "Participant-level Spearman correlation of MRS with baseline pTau"
)
```

## Plot

```{r scatter_inputs}
scatter_panel_labels <- make_scatter_panel_labels(mrs_group_summary, mrs_levels)
scatter_plot_df <- add_panel_column(scatter_participants, scatter_panel_labels)
spearman_plot_labels <- add_panel_column(spearman_results, scatter_panel_labels)
```

```{r scatter_mrs_baseline_ptau, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5}
scatter_mrs_ptau <- make_mrs_ptau_scatter_plot(
  scatter_plot_df, spearman_plot_labels, make_scatter_caption(),
  mrs_cutoff = mrs_median, mrs_levels = mrs_levels
)
scatter_mrs_ptau
```

# Comparison by MRS

These comparisons use the **same Low MRS and High MRS median split**
as the two mixed models. Baseline characteristics are counted once per
participant; follow-up summaries use the observations included in the models.
Continuous characteristics are compared with a two-group Kruskal-Wallis
test, and categorical characteristics with Fisher's exact test.

```{r comparison_by_mrs_setup}
mrs_comparison_participants <- get_baseline_rows(mrs_model_df)
check_finite_mrs(mrs_comparison_participants)
```

## Follow-up and visits

```{r comparison_by_mrs_followup}
mrs_followup <- summarize_followup(mrs_model_df)
mrs_followup_table <- summarize_mrs_continuous(
  mrs_followup,
  c(followup_years = "Follow-up from baseline (years)",
    n_visits = "Number of modeled visit times"),
  mrs_levels
)
knitr::kable(
  mrs_followup_table,
  caption = "Follow-up by low/high MRS group: participant N and mean ± SD (median)."
)
```

## Continuous baseline characteristics

```{r comparison_by_mrs_continuous}
mrs_baseline_table <- summarize_mrs_continuous(
  mrs_comparison_participants,
  c(baseline_age = "Baseline age (years)",
    PHC_Education = "Education (years)",
    baseline_pTau = "Baseline pTau"),
  mrs_levels
)
knitr::kable(
  mrs_baseline_table,
  caption = "Baseline characteristics by low/high MRS group: participant N and mean ± SD (median)."
)
```

## Categorical baseline characteristics

```{r comparison_by_mrs_categorical}
mrs_categorical_table <- summarize_mrs_categorical(
  mrs_comparison_participants,
  c(PHC_Sex = "Sex", APOE4 = "APOE ε4 allele count"),
  mrs_levels
)
knitr::kable(
  mrs_categorical_table,
  caption = paste0(
    "Categorical baseline characteristics by low/high MRS group: n (% within group). ",
    "Total N and group N are nonmissing participant denominators; ",
    "Fisher P compares the two MRS groups and is repeated for each level."
  )
)
```
